Reason: The lateral view (Figure 1b) localizes the mass to the posterior mediastinum/paravertebral region, and its borders appear well-defined and lobulated rather than infiltrative. This morphology is characteristic of benign posterior mediastinal masses (e.g., neurogenic tumors) which typically compress adjacent structures without invading them.
